messages:
mira: Noticed a sharp Xid 13/31 uptick on a subset of a10s in us-east1 around 03:20 UTC. Looks like it aligns with tenant eviction waves, plus NIC netqueue backlog spikes.

sre-bot: Alert: XID_31_RATE_HIGH on rack-us-east1-r42 (cards: 3/16) — sample window 5m. See /alerts/3412345678

jasper: Can you paste the narrowed query? want tenant IDs and evict timestamps.

mira: Query pinned down to tenant: cloud-batch-47 and a handful of small-tenants sharing same top-of-rack. Results:
```
select tenant_id, count(*) as xids, avg(netqueue_depth)
from gpu_xid_events
where xid in (13,31) and region='us-east1' and ts > now()-interval '1 hour'
group by tenant_id
order by xids desc
-- output: cloud-batch-47: 210 xids, avg netqueue_depth 84
-- small-tenant-9: 42 xids, avg netqueue_depth 78
```

olivia: That netqueue depth is alarming. Xid 31 often follows NIC timeouts and packet drops. Are we seeing NIC errors or soft-drain churn?

mira: Yes, soft-drain events spike at same time. Eviction controller logs show rapid eviction loops due to transient IO pressure on the shared nodes.

kai: Hypothesis: eviction churn causes PCIe/NIC DMA queues to flush unpredictably -> kernel/NVIDIA driver sees timeouts -> Xid 31/13. Also could be K8s pod reschedule thrash increasing interrupt load.

nate-oncall: @mira can you run a quick repro: pin that tenant to a different rack or disable eviction controller for the tenant for 10m and see if xids stop? I'll coordinate a controlled soft-drain on one affected host.

mira: Will try a temporary placement override for cloud-batch-47 to rack-us-east1-r55 (lower colocation). Also filtering logs for NIC drops during the window:
```
Mar 20 03:19:42 host42 kernel: mlx5_core 0000:65:00.0: mlx5_qp_err: QP 12 state ERR, opcode RX, syndrome EQD_TIMEOUT
Mar 20 03:19:43 host42 nvidia: Xid 31 GPU:3 PID:12891 T:2026-03-20 03:19:43
Mar 20 03:19:47 host42 dockerd: container restart tenant=cloud-batch-47
```

jasper: Good correlation. Two actionable items: 1) throttle eviction controller to increase grace period for GPUs under net saturation, 2) add netqueue depth alert to preemptively block evictions.

olivia: Agreed. Also add a temporary driver-level guard: when netqueue_depth>70, suppress immediate soft-drain and prefer autoscale fallback. Could we update node-evict controller config?

kai: We should test whether Xid 13 is decode-time ECC or TLS handshake noise — but current logs point to DMA timeouts (NIC). Xid 13 sometimes shows on decode when packets lost mid-stream.

nate-oncall: I'm starting a controlled soft-drain on host42 now (only index 3) and moving cloud-batch-47 off one card to see effect. Will report in ~5m. :hourglass_flowing_sand:
